body:
## Summary
The notes-and-versions pad (useVersions.ts, 455 lines) is a state machine written as ten useState cells, three refs and six `if (running)` guards. Nothing stamps it: its accepted chains do not record which notebook they were written against. This card moves every transition into a pure `padState.ts` reducer with four phases (idle, starting, running, staged). The hook becomes a thin shell over it for persistence and the turn ledger. The record is stamped with the active source's digest, so a ledger written on another notebook is held as an orphan, the same way the scope already is.

## Description
The hook's header promises three rules: feedback aggregates; one run at a time, with no notes added mid-flight; and a candidate is not the baseline until it is accepted. Today guard clauses scattered through the callbacks enforce them, and a ref enforces exactly-once landing. The Node probe lane can execute none of this; the two existing tests of the hook grep its source text. The reducer turns the rules into a transition table the lane can drive. The hook keeps only what must be React: load and save, the resumeTurn/getTurn effects, and the preview.

The digest stamp closes a hole the C1 work left open. The scope is digest-stamped and orphan-aware (useScope.ts:34-47), but the version ledger stacked on it is not. A creator who accepts v2 on the replay and then reasons their own notebook keeps v2 as the baseline, keeps pad notes keyed to the old cards, and the next recalibration sends v2's chain beside the new notebook. The stamp is also the seam compose (script-phase-B stage 3) will need: once renders are per-notebook, a ledger has to say which base it edits.

## Flow
- padState.ts: `PadState`, `PadAction`, `padReduce`, `padRecordOf`, and `padBasis(record, digest)` returning {baseline, notes, orphan}.
- useVersions.ts: a single `useReducer(padReduce)`. Load runs the stored record through padBasis with `ctx.source.digest`. Accept dispatches with the digest. land, run and cancel each dispatch an action. The returned API shape does not change, so StickyNotebook, VersionBar, ScriptStep and NotesContext need no edits.
- records.ts: adds `ScriptVersionsData.digest?: string`. parse rejects a digest that is not a string.
- RecalibrateControl.tsx: an orphaned ledger renders as one line with a `<StaleBadge>` carrying the count of held versions and notes. No prose slot.

## Expected impact
The pad's rules become test cases rather than comments. A whole class of defect (a guard missed in one callback) closes, and so does the notebook-switch hole. Compose gets a ledger it can key to its draft.

## Evaluation
Claim: every pad rule, and the orphan rule, is executable as a pure transition.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (padState.ts does not exist; the record has no digest)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - write tests/golden-path/script-pad-state.probe.spec.ts first; keep the turn-recalibrate, c1-closing, recalibration-stacks, script-sticky-pad, chain-break-reaches-the-reviewer and step-verdicts probes green, along with npm run typecheck and check:kit-census
Result: better
Gate: architecture

title: Walkable version history: staged runs survive reload, any version restores forward
shared_surfaces: app/_phases/script/useVersions.ts and records.ts (also in slot A: if both are built, B goes after A and rebases)

receiptOf(restoreAs(v2, v4, 'v5', 9)) === 'restored from v2 · no model call', not the 'simulated locally' line a fallback gets
stagedOf(candidate, 'v3') round-trips through SCRIPT_VERSIONS.parse, and resumeStaged(parsed.staged, {baselineId:'v3'}) returns a Version deep-equal to the candidate, engineRun and manifest included

After a reload, resumeTurn answers 'none' (lib/turns/client.ts:244) and the paid plan is never staged again, although the turn record still holds it (lib/turns/ledger.ts:20-22, 'The RESULT is kept')

app/_phases/script/versions.ts:291-328 - a run is a paid model turn whose cost, duration and model the receipt carries. That cost is what a reload discards
app/_phases/script/useVersions.ts:345-355 - accept only appends to `accepted`, and nothing leads back to an earlier version. Accepting also clears the notes that produced it
app/_phases/script/_matrix/VersionBar.tsx:60-73 - with no candidate staged, the bar names only the current baseline. The accepted list (useVersions.ts:57) is never drawn as a history
app/_phases/script/versions.ts:291-293 - receiptOf has two branches for versions with no model call and cannot say 'restored'

app/_phases/script/ScriptStep.tsx:329-349 and _notes/RecalibrateControl.tsx:172-186 - a staged candidate is already re-gated (`reading` is the candidate) and accept already carries the two-click override receipt, so a restored version passes the same gate with no new gate code

runner_up: Let VersionBar pick any two accepted versions to compare on Coverage and Spend, not only baseline against the staged candidate.

body:
## Summary
The one loop in this step that costs money has two blind spots. A recalibration the creator has not yet accepted vanishes on reload: what remains is a 'lost' line with no action, although the plan still sits in the turn ledger. And accepting is one-way: once v3 is the baseline, nothing leads back to v2. This card persists the staged candidate against the baseline it was built on, and adds forward-only restore. Restoring vN stages it as a new candidate, which goes through the same gate and accept/override path as any run.

## Description
The comment at useVersions.ts:42-48 refused to persist staging because restoring one 'would put an unreviewed result back on the pad as if it had been decided'. That reason holds for restoring it as a BASELINE. Restoring it as the staged CANDIDATE leaves it undecided: the candidate bar, the re-run gate and the two-click override still stand between it and the baseline. The only guard it needs is that the baseline it was built on has not moved. If it has, the candidate is reported lost, with that reason.

Restore follows the registry's restore-semantics rule. Restoring vN mints vM with `restoredFrom: vN`, staged as a candidate, and nothing is truncated. A restore can be undone by another restore, so the version list becomes somewhere to try things, and the 'accepted over the gate' receipts on later versions are kept.

## Flow
- history.ts (pure): `restoreAs(v, baseline, id, at)`, `stagedOf(candidate, baselineId)`, `resumeStaged(staged, {baselineId})`, `acceptInto(accepted, v)`.
- versions.ts: adds `Version.restoredFrom?: string`, and gives `receiptOf` a third no-model branch.
- records.ts: parses `ScriptVersionsData.staged?`. A damaged staged entry is dropped and reported, and `accepted` is kept.
- useVersions.ts: the save writes `stagedOf(candidate)` and the load resumes it through `resumeStaged`. A new `restore(id)` is exposed and refused while a run is live.
- VersionBar.tsx: with no candidate staged, the accepted versions render as a row of chips. Each chip shows its label, its restored-from provenance as a `<Provenance>`, and its receipt and override lines, and every chip except the current one has a restore action. No explanatory slot.
- RecalibrateControl.tsx: the 'lost' line remains only for a staged run that could not be resumed, and now gives its reason (baseline moved, or unreadable).

## Expected impact
A reload no longer loses a paid, minutes-long answer. Undoing an accept takes one click, and that click can itself be undone. Creators can step through versions on Coverage and Spend instead of being locked to the newest one.

## Evaluation
Claim: a staged run survives a reload, and any accepted version can be restored forward through the existing gate.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (history.ts does not exist; there is no staged persistence and no restoredFrom)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - write tests/golden-path/script-version-history.probe.spec.ts first; keep the recalibration-stacks, turn-recalibrate, script-sticky-pad, script-tab-tallies and chain-break-reaches-the-reviewer probes green, along with typecheck, check:narration and check:kit-census; capture the studio-script screen in both worlds with cx-capture
Result: better
Gate: none
